paragraphs: How Electricity Reaches Our House, posted by Lily. Guide Ann came to the school library on Thursday after lunch. She brought a laptop and a plastic comb. Mia took the photos, and I wrote this page. Here is her diagram with four steps. Many children came, and the library was full.

Guide Ann showed the diagram on the laptop screen. Step one is the factory, and it makes electricity. Step two is the wires. They carry the electricity over the roads and the fields. Some wires are very high, and some are under the ground. Step three is the meter. At our house, the meter is in the garage, next to the bikes. It shows how much electricity we use. Step four is the light. We push a switch, and the lamp comes on. A lamp in our house uses very little electricity. "Electricity moves very fast," said Guide Ann.

Then Guide Ann did a quick experiment. We sat on cushions on the floor around her table. She rubbed the plastic comb on her hair for ten seconds. Then she held the comb over some small pieces of paper. The pieces were very thin. The pieces jumped up and stuck to the comb! "Wow!" said everybody. "This is a little electricity, and it is safe," said Guide Ann. Mia tried it, and her comb picked up three pieces. Leo tried it, too, but his comb picked up only one piece. Everybody laughed.

Big electricity is a danger for your health. Never touch a wire or a plug with wet hands. If a wire is broken, tell an adult. Keep water away from the laptop, too. Do not play with plugs. A safe home is good for your health. "Turn off the light when you leave a room," said Guide Ann. "That saves electricity and money."

Which step is new for you? Where is the meter at your home? Look for a small box on a wall. Guide Ann will visit us again next month. We want to ask her about the sun and the wind. Tell us in a message!
